title: Order refund posting to the ledger
name: Order refund service

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code splits a refund across order lines and records it in the ledger? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
A client times out and re-sends refund_order with the same order_id and request_id after the first call had fully completed. What happens on the second call?
choices: The gateway is called again with the same idempotency key, and the ledger posts a second set of entries.
It raises RefundExceedsCaptured whenever the first call refunded the full captured amount.
It returns the same ref immediately, without calling the gateway or touching the ledger or the order.
It re-runs the allocation and updates refunded_cents again, but the unique ref stops the ledger insert.

questions.prompt: The process is killed right after self._gateway.refund(...) returns successfully but before the with-block commits. The client retries with the same request_id. What is the outcome?
choices: The retry reuses the same idempotency key, so the gateway does not refund twice, and the ledger and order are then written.
The retry is rejected because the gateway has already refunded the charge.
The retry issues a second refund at the gateway, because the ledger has no record of the first.
The retry returns early because the gateway call counts as having completed the request.

questions.prompt: Ledger.post() never commits, and RefundService calls it inside `with self._conn:` together with the UPDATE on orders. What does this arrangement ensure?
choices: Concurrent refunds on the same order are serialized by the ledger insert.
The gateway refund is rolled back if the ledger insert fails.
Each ledger entry is committed separately, so a partial refund can be recorded line by line.
The refunded_cents update and the ledger transaction with its entries commit together or not at all.
